title: Remove first-use Computer Use App authorization for ordinary actions
hypothesis: An explicit user-requested default-access policy removes unnecessary App authorization interruptions without bypassing effective tiers, explicit denials, sensitive-action confirmation or foreground takeover consent.
measurement: No model/provider calls. Two new real BrokerCore cases for headless root/child sessions fail on public baseline cc733385 with approval_unavailable, then pass with the change, granting a lease without an approval event or persisted user grant. The complete component run passes 334/336 before dev dependencies are installed; the two compiler-dependent failures are missing compiler infrastructure, and both pass on rerun with the declared TypeScript 7 dependency (all five compiler controls pass). Full component typecheck passes. Focused policy/approval/authority/external-open cases pass, archive/identity/signature checks pass 11/11, and default/full public-runtime smoke exits 0. The new cases also pass 2/2 against the actual extracted .rotom.8 archive. All eight native prebuilt files are byte-identical to .rotom.7.
result: Shipped source default: ordinary App access does not ask for a first-use App grant, including child/headless sessions. Existing explicit deny/tier limits, sensitive labels, external file/App opens, foreground takeover confirmation, broker arbitration and user stop remain intact. Product component version/integrity/archive pins are synchronized to 0.5.1-rotom.8. No live installation/helper was overwritten, no desktop write was performed, and real Preview interaction remains unverified. This is a deterministic implementation of a user-requested policy change, not a model-quality or token/cost optimization; model-driven gates were not run. Expected harvest impact is fewer unnecessary user-decision interruptions; aggregate impact remains unmeasured.
